reference_boards.title: Apple cinematic restraint
reference_boards.blurb: High craft, cultural ambition, sparse copy. Style bar for tech that feels like film.

items.title: 1984 (print campaign origin concept)
items.style_notes: Abandoned print concept that seeded the TV film: individuals vs monster computers of big business/government.
Desaturated dystopian industrial palette with scarlet athletic accent; Blade Runner-adjacent cinematic dystopia.

items.title: Here's to the Crazy Ones
items.style_notes: B&W archival montage of icons over poetic VO (Jobs and Richard Dreyfuss versions circulated).

items.title: Think Different
items.style_notes: Black-and-white portraiture of cultural icons with spare typography and the incomplete Think different. lockup.

items.title: iPod Silhouettes
items.style_notes: Flat colour fields, black dancing silhouettes, white earbuds and iPod as the only product highlight.

items.title: Get a Mac
items.style_notes: White cyclorama two-hander: Justin Long as Mac vs John Hodgman as PC in deadpan sketch format.

reference_boards.title: Absolut print surrealism
reference_boards.blurb: One bottle, infinite art directions. Long-running print systems as style DNA.

items.title: Absolut Perfection
items.style_notes: Haloed bottle on black—two-word Absolut ____ headline template that launched a 25-year print empire.

items.title: Absolut Perfection (bottle campaign origin)
items.style_notes: Product-as-concept system: bottle silhouette as hero with two-word Absolut X headline formula.

items.title: Absolut Bottle Campaign (ongoing print system)
items.style_notes: Infinite bottle-as-canvas variations—cityscapes, fashion, art commissions—always resolving to the bottle shape.

items.title: Absolut Warhol
items.style_notes: Warhol's painted Absolut bottle—first of the artist series.

items.title: Absolut Haring
items.style_notes: Haring's pop-line interpretation of the Absolut bottle.

items.title: Absolut Ruscha
items.style_notes: Bottle shadow as a wolf—Ruscha's desert-pop take on the Absolut canvas.

reference_boards.title: Nike belief & culture
reference_boards.blurb: Athlete as myth, social tension as brand fuel. W+K lineage.

items.title: Just Do It
items.style_notes: Tagline-first system uniting disparate athletic spots; first TV execution featured octogenarian runner Walt Stack.

items.title: Just Do It — Walt Stack
items.style_notes: 80-year-old runner Walt Stack crossing Golden Gate—grit over glamour as the first Just Do It TV face.

items.title: Find Your Greatness
items.style_notes: Documentary-real athletic moments in ordinary places (not London venues), counter-programming Olympic spectacle.

items.title: Breaking2
items.style_notes: Live-attempt documentary aesthetic: Monza track, paced formation running, science-lab production design around Eliud Kipchoge.

items.title: Dream Crazy
items.style_notes: Athletic montage anchored by Colin Kaepernick VO; high-production sports cinematography with social-issue gravity.

items.title: Dream Crazy — Believe in something
items.style_notes: Colin Kaepernick portrait with Believe in something. Even if it means sacrificing everything. copy lockup.

reference_boards.title: Fashion provocation
reference_boards.blurb: Gucci / Dior / Chanel / Marc Jacobs — image-led desire over product demo.

items.title: Prada Fall/Winter 1996-1998 campaigns (Glen Luchford)
items.style_notes: Cinematic, narrative fashion photography—Amber Valletta and actor casting as art-house ads.

items.title: YSL Opium (Sophie Dahl)
items.style_notes: Reclining nude with gold jewelry and green eyeshadow on fur—high-fashion nude as outdoor poster.

items.title: Yves Saint Laurent Tom Ford-era campaigns (2000-2004)
items.style_notes: Hyper-sexualised high-fashion print language continuing Ford's Gucci shock aesthetic at YSL.

items.title: Gucci Spring/Summer 2003 ('G' pubic hair ad)
items.style_notes: Ultra-close crop with pubic hair shaved into a Gucci G—shock fashion print.

items.title: No. 5 The Film
items.style_notes: Three-minute Baz Luhrmann mini-movie with Nicole Kidman; Moulin Rouge opulence compressed into perfume myth.

items.title: No. 5 the Film
items.style_notes: Three-minute Moulin Rouge-scale branded short with Nicole Kidman as a perfume-world celebrity.

items.title: J'adore (Charlize Theron / Nick Knight)
items.style_notes: Gold-draped Charlize Theron as goddess of J'adore—Galliano glamour via Nick Knight.

items.title: J'adore (Charlize Theron)
items.style_notes: Golden liquid light, Charlize Theron descending into liquid gold; Mondino high-glamour perfume cinema.

reference_boards.title: UK craft storytelling
reference_boards.blurb: John Lewis, Cadbury, Guinness — patience, music, narrative payoff.

items.title: Happiness is a cigar called Hamlet
items.style_notes: Embarrassing mishap + consoling cigar + Loussier Bach—comic British understatement.

items.title: The Milk Tray Man (Man in Black)
items.style_notes: Black-clad adventurer delivers Milk Tray against impossible odds—and all because the lady loves Milk Tray.

items.title: Benson & Hedges (gold pack / surreal posters)
items.style_notes: People-free surreal still lifes of the gold pack—Mousehole among the classics.

items.title: Silk Cut (slashed purple silk posters)
items.style_notes: Wordless purple silk slash (Fontana-inspired)—brand recognized by colour and cut alone.

items.title: Launderette (501)
items.style_notes: Nick Kamen strips to boxers in a 1950s launderette; period Americana set to Marvin Gaye.

items.title: The Economist (White Out of Red posters)
items.style_notes: White type on Economist red—witty one-liners implying smart advantage.

items.title: Good Things Come to Those Who Wait
items.style_notes: Platform line spanning Surfer, Swimblack, noitulovE—patience as brand theatre.

items.title: Surfer
items.style_notes: High-contrast B&W Hawaiian surf mythos; white-horse metamorphosis VFX over Leftfield score; Melville-tinged VO.

items.style_notes: Artist interpretations of Great Books quotations—corporate ads as cultural patronage.

items.title: Think Small
items.style_notes: Vast white space, tiny Beetle photo, self-deprecating headline; Swiss-influenced minimalist print layout.

items.title: Lemon
items.style_notes: Same Think Small system—single Beetle photo, one-word headline Lemon, long body copy about factory rejection.

items.title: We Try Harder
items.style_notes: Honest No.2 positioning—large headline, small visual, Perpetua type reverse of convention.

items.title: IBM Identity / Think (Paul Rand era)
items.style_notes: Eight-bar IBM logo and rigorous corporate graphic system; modernist clarity over ornament.
